abstract.p: Synthetic fixture article used only by the offline A5 acquisition tests.

sec.title: Introduction
sec.p: This synthetic record exists so that the offline A5 acquisition tests can drive one fetch through the canonical candidate loop and the A6 content validation step without any network access. Total neoadjuvant therapy has become a common strategy for locally advanced rectal cancer, and the choice between induction chemotherapy and consolidation chemotherapy remains an open question in everyday practice.

sec.title: Methods
sec.p: The fixture body is written to exceed the centrally defined minimum body length so that A6 classifies it as parseable content rather than as a truncated artifact. No real record, patient or measurement is described here, and the numbers below carry no clinical meaning whatsoever.

sec.title: Results
sec.p: Thirty synthetic records were processed end to end by the offline fixtures. Twenty-eight produced a validated body, one was rejected because its declared identifier contradicted the canonical metadata, and one was rejected because the extracted body was shorter than the required minimum.

sec.title: Discussion
sec.p: Keeping the acquisition fixtures small and deterministic makes it possible to assert the exact failure stage for each candidate, which is why this document intentionally repeats the same synthetic statements in slightly different wording throughout the body sections.
